Subject: Humetix — pricing & latency follow-up

Hi Oliver / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the clear signal on priorities. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a scoped PoC and price estimate.

Call highlights (what I heard)
- Primary product: live customer support chat + short-form summarization in the agent UI.
- Expected steady state: ~120M tokens / month (inference tokens).
- Peak/burst: up to ~6M tokens / day on promotional days (2–3x baseline daily traffic).
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for chat responses; tail latency is a priority for UX.
- Budget range: you mentioned a target of roughly $40–$55 per 1M tokens as a preferred unit economics range.

Initial positioning and trade-offs
- Hosted Pro (fastest path): lowest time to value. For p95 200ms we recommend streaming responses + low-latency routing. This gives quick onboarding but the per-1M token price is usually higher than reserved capacity.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): if you can commit to a monthly spend, the amortized unit cost drops significantly and we can meet p95 targets consistently for sustained traffic. Dedicated also provides isolation for compliance reasons.
- Hybrid approach: PoC on Hosted with streaming and prefix caching; transition to Dedicated once volume is predictable to capture lower unit costs.

Latency vs cost knobs (short)
- Streaming vs batching: streaming minimizes tail latency at higher cost; batching reduces unit cost but increases response tail.
- Batching window and max batch size are SLO-tunable knobs we can control per-route.
- KV / prefix caching: will materially reduce token consumption for repeated prompts (agents + historical context).
- Quantization: int8/4-bit quantized variants reduce GPU memory and cost; often yields ~20–40% cost improvements with small quality tradeoffs depending on model.

Next steps I propose
1) I attached the redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf and SLA tier matrix — review.
2) We'll run a short architecture deep-dive with Dev (solutions) to map SLOs -> config (streaming/batching/kv/quantization). Can you do Tue 2/17 or Wed 2/18?
3) Share your monthly volume projection file (you can attach the spreadsheet or give a HubSpot forecast) and confirm target $/1M token band (so we can produce a tailored cost estimate).
4) We'll follow with a formal PoC proposal + timeline and an optional Dedicated capacity bid if you want committed pricing.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf (pricing summary), sla_tier_matrix.csv (SLA / latency tiers).

Thanks — feel free to reply inline.

Cheers,

Hi all — looping in some quick technical tradeoffs and cost math so we can align estimates to Oliver's p95 <=180ms goal. I'll keep it pragmatic.

Assumptions I used:
- Model: medium-size chat model equivalent (context 2k tokens average per request).
- Baseline: 120M tokens/month (~4M/day average), peak bursts up to 6M/day.
- Target quality: streaming + quantized weights acceptable for this product.

Options and expected unit economics (very high level):
A) Hosted Pro (streaming, single-tenant routing)
   - Cost per 1M tokens (streaming-optimized): roughly $60–$75 (depends on actual mix of generation vs embeddings).
   - Pros: fastest onboarding, no infra commitment, turnkey telemetry.
   - Cons: higher marginal cost on sustained volume.

B) Dedicated reserved GPU pool (12mo commit), optimized for low tail latency (streaming + low-latency kernels)
   - Amortized cost per 1M tokens: ~$30–$42 depending on commit band (we'd need commit tiers; ballpark for 120M/mo it's toward the lower end after amortization).
   - Pros: stable p95, lower unit cost, isolation for compliance.
   - Cons: requires commit and lead time to provision (1–3 weeks to finalize infra and validation).

C) Hybrid (start Hosted PoC, then move to Dedicated)
   - PoC (2–4 weeks): hosted; validate traffic profile, measure cache hit rate.
   - If cache hit rates >20–30% and steady traffic looks durable, move to Dedicated and drop unit cost by ~30–50%.

Latency knobs (practical guidance)
- Streaming: required for <200ms p95 in most cases. Use small streaming chunks and prioritize single-request routing.
- Batching: only for non-interactive routes. If you batch chat, p95 will worsen. We can set per-route batching windows.
- KV / prefix caching: strongly recommended — will reduce tokens and tail latency for repeated contexts (agents referencing ticket history).
- Quantization: int8 or 4-bit will reduce GPU footprint and cost substantially with small model-quality impact; good fit for chat.

Capacity and burst handling
- For bursts up to 6M/day, Dedicated with a configured burst pool or autoscaling buffer is best; alternatively, Hosted has flexible bursts but costs more.

Concrete next deliverables from us
1) I'll prepare two back-of-envelope scenarios with explicit math for (A) Hosted streaming and (B) Dedicated 12mo commit (include token bands: 0–50M, 50–150M, >150M).
2) We'll include estimated p95 numbers for the config and call out which knobs must remain fixed to preserve SLO.
3) Suggest an architecture session (30–45 min) for Tue 2/17 11:00 PT or Wed 2/18 09:00 PT — pick one and we'll lock it.

Happy to include more detail in the formal proposal.
